solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Definite reassignment of vice-consul

indicators.note: a reassignment hands the letters of the diplomat's title new positions, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomatic posting is changed once and for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conclusive settles the matter, so it is definite: a synonym.

clue.text: Rude apprentice blocked by church

indicators.note: the word for apprentice has the church abbreviation stuck in its middle, blocking it

parts.note: to indent someone is to bind them by indenture, as an apprentice
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A trainee behaves crudely and is stopped by the church authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprentice' is a verb here: to indent is to bind someone by indenture as an apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent behaviour or language is rude in the sense of offensive or improper: a synonym.

clue.text: Flowering plant completely surrounded by work on lawn

indicators.note: the lawn-cutting word goes round the word for completely, so it surrounds it

parts.note: to mow is to cut grass
all means completely, as in 'all alone'

explanation.surface: A garden flower is entirely hemmed in by someone cutting the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallow is a pink-flowered plant of the genus Malva: an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Caledonian guide losing half of us

indicators.note: the word for guide drops a letter, losing it

parts.note: a scout guides or reconnoitres ahead of others

indicators.note: one of the two letters of 'us' is half of it

explanation.surface: A Scottish guide leaves half of our group behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a native of that country.

clue.text: Like Vesuvius — very conical, erupting

indicators.note: erupting things burst apart, so the letters of conical are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Mount Vesuvius, a steep cone, is erupting.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius is an active volcano near Naples, so anything like it is of a volcano: description by example.

clue.text: Rural firm to withdraw effort?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a made-up verb: to un-try would be to withdraw a try, an effort; the question mark flags the invention

explanation.surface: A rural business asks whether it should stop trying.
explanation.walkthrough: UNTRY is no real word: the question mark licenses reading 'un-try' as undoing an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in country lanes, it means belonging to the countryside: a synonym for rural.

clue.text: Hard work: load upset about setter planning organised movement

parts.note: a chore is a tedious, hard task

indicators.note: the overturned load goes about the setter's name, enclosing it
in a down clue, upset turns the word for load upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: cargo is a ship's load
the setter of this puzzle is Phi

explanation.surface: Tough work: a load is overturned around the puzzle setter while a dance is being planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' is this puzzle's compiler, whose pseudonym is Phi; in a down clue 'upset' turns the load upside down before it goes about him.
explanation.definitionFit: Choreography is the planning of dance steps, so the adjective describes the arranging of organised movement.

clue.text: Prominent entrances to creature habitats in reserve

parts.note: a star is a prominent, leading figure; used attributively, as in star performer

indicators.note: the entrances to words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Eye-catching gateways lead into animal enclosures in a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a nature reserve in the surface, but it means stiffness of manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is stiff formality of manner, so it equals reserve in the sense of aloofness.

clue.text: Dodgy character captures hearts in Channel Island

indicators.note: the island name holds the card-suit letter, capturing it

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands
H is the abbreviation for hearts in cards

explanation.surface: A crook on Sark wins hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark is a swindler or predatory dealer, so a dodgy character: a figurative sense.

clue.text: Copper's put in excellent report for crime?

indicators.note: the chemical symbol with its S is placed inside the word for excellent

parts.note: ace means excellent
CU is the chemical symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A police officer is put into a superb crime report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with an offence is to report them for a crime: a paraphrase, marked by the question mark.

clue.text: Easy to get nothing, tipster's favourite being tardy

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
a nap is a racing tipster's best tip of the day
late means tardy

explanation.surface: Easy money is lost because the horse a tipster fancied comes in late.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handed to you on a plate is obtained without effort: an idiom for easy to get.

clue.text: Relent, showing embroidery in pleat in sweater?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for pleat

parts.note: a tuck is a stitched fold or pleat in fabric

indicators.note: embroidering a story adds fanciful changes, so the letters of the word are worked into new order

explanation.surface: Someone gives in, embroidering a pleat on a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing embroidery' scrambles the six letters of 'Relent', and 'in' puts that scramble between the first two and last two letters of the pleat word.
explanation.definitionFit: A turtleneck is a high-collared jumper, so an example of a sweater; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: British writer losing some love for seducer

indicators.note: the writer's name gives up part of itself, the letter for love

parts.note: Virginia Woolf was an English novelist
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An English author loses some affection for a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is slang for a man who predatorily pursues women: a synonym for seducer.

clue.text: Phone tapper working inter-lines

indicators.note: working means set in motion, so the letters of the hyphenated word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper is busy between telephone lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eavesdrops on telephone calls is a phone tapper: a synonym.

clue.text: Girl idly forgetting city map

indicators.note: the word for idly forgets a pair of its letters, dropping them

parts.note: lazily means idly
an A-Z is a street atlas of a British city, especially London

explanation.surface: A girl lazily forgets her street map.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a British book of street maps for a city, so 'city map' gives AZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily is a female first name, so it fits a girl: an example.

clue.text: Row of stadium welcoming good keen player

indicators.note: the row of seats takes in the letter for good, welcoming it

parts.note: a tier is a row of seating in a stadium

explanation.surface: A row of the stands welcomes a fine, eager sportsperson.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a tiger is a fierce, determined competitor, so a keen player: a figurative sense.

clue.text: Plant came up, beginning to revive in spring month

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, came up

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the month's name

parts.note: May is a month of spring

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A plant sprouted, starting to recover in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic shrub used as a herb: an example of a plant.

clue.text: To try to catch female is hard

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Trying to win over a woman is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle for something is to try to catch it, literally with rod and line or figuratively.

clue.text: Fine reduces for a bunch?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
lowers means reduces, as with prices

explanation.surface: A court cuts its penalty for a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty, but it is the abbreviation F.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of blooms is a bouquet; the question mark marks the definition as by example.

clue.text: Side offers food for thought, switching wingers

indicators.note: the wingers of a word are its outer letters, and switching them swaps the first and last

parts.note: meat is the substance of an argument, the food for thought

explanation.surface: A football side provides ideas worth chewing over, changing its wide players round.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the outer letters of MEAT, its 'wingers', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in sport is a group of players playing together: a synonym.

clue.text: Strong, masculine and significant, dismissing our side

parts.note: M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

indicators.note: the word for significant sends away a pair of its letters

parts.note: weighty means significant, important
we is our side, us

explanation.surface: A powerful, manly and important opponent knocks out our team.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means very powerful, so it is a synonym for strong.

clue.text: Waters rose, spoiling US building

indicators.note: spoiling messes up the two words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Floodwater rose and damaged an American building.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chicago skyscraper, now Willis Tower, was long the world's tallest building: an example.

clue.text: Untrustworthy character in Sweden uncovered cut

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

indicators.note: the word for uncovered is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: naked means uncovered

explanation.surface: A treacherous person in Sweden is caught bare and wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass is a treacherous person, so the word means an untrustworthy character.

clue.text: Opening words: "What about rude fellow getting charge?"

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about the two other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning 'what?'
a pig is an ill-mannered, rude person
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what happens about a boorish man being charged.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigraph is a quotation set at the start of a book or chapter: its opening words.

clue.text: Old English used in premier piece of literature

indicators.note: the language abbreviation is used inside the leader's initials

parts.note: PM is Prime Minister, the premier

explanation.surface: Anglo-Saxon is used in a leading literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem is a written composition in verse: an example of a piece of literature.

clue.text: More restrained cry of fright, landing in sea at Calais

indicators.note: the cry lands inside the French word, going within it

parts.note: mer is French for sea, Calais being a French port
eek is a cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A milder yelp of fear is heard as something lands in the Channel off Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: Meek people are submissive and quiet, so the comparative means more restrained.

clue.text: Car's front of bonnet, say — covering one removed

indicators.note: say asks for the letter as it is spoken, its name
the front of a word is its first letter
the covering word has the letter for one taken out

parts.note: a tile is a roof covering
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A car's bonnet front, for instance, has had its cover taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of bonnet' is B, and 'say' asks for its name, BEE. TILE minus I gives TLE. The 'bonnet' is the car's engine cover, misleading towards the car's front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Volkswagen Beetle is a famous small car: an example.

clue.text: Thriller writer's chief character ultimately is Bond

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: a tie is a bond, something that binds

explanation.surface: A spy novelist's lead figure turns out in the end to be James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is simply a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote detective thrillers: an example of a thriller writer.
